entries.title: Where Steering Signals Come From: Activation Source Selection in Activation Steering
entries.method: Holds intervention/construction/search protocol fixed while varying source context and readout; tests relation tasks and projection removal of an execution-aligned component.
entries.result: Boundary-state sources outperform answer-bearing averages in these protocols; removal reduces steering. Source-position effects alone are already covered.
entries.limit: Best-over-grid steering potential is not proof that a particular native neuron implements a semantic variable.

entries.title: Representation Without Control: Testing the Realization Effect in Language Models
entries.method: Train-only mean direction with held-out status readout and downstream wager/risk steering; separate classification diagnostic has broader data and a duplicated-instruction caveat.
entries.result: Readable status does not yield reliable sign-symmetric behavior control in the tested setup.
entries.limit: Replicating detector/effector dissociation in one more task is insufficient novelty.

entries.title: Stress-Testing Random-Vector Controls for Activation Steering
entries.method: Reproduces a released GPT-2-XL comparison then redraws 20 norm-matched controls; separate configuration and incorrect-index audits.
entries.result: Control ordering varies by realization; batch/attention changes and shared hook/readout indexing can alter distributional metrics.
entries.limit: These are distinct case studies; they do not establish semantic steering or an isolated universal noise floor.

entries.title: SPARK: Susceptibility-Guided Profiling and Steering of Latent Reasoning States in Large Language Models
entries.method: Embedding-noise response intensity is residualized against log length; combines cross-layer coordination with calibration-chosen anchors and layer selection.
entries.result: Reports held-out benchmark gains with calibrated steering. Generic input susceptibility and length adjustment are already covered.
entries.limit: Cross-intervention forecasting and evidence for a shared causal factor are separate questions, not implied by these results.

entries.title: A Geometric Account of Activation Steering through Angle–Norm Decomposition
entries.method: Compares six operations with matched angular targets or mean concept scores and separately changes radial scale across seven models.
entries.result: Angular information and radial stability can dissociate; modest norm growth can improve generation stability at matched angle.
entries.limit: A norm-only causal interpretation or a new name for normalized steering is not novel.

entries.title: What Does Activation Steering Control? Attribution Across Answer Encodings and Output-Sensitive Subspaces
entries.method: Freezes intervention while remapping labels, identifiers and rows; uses 108 factorial conditions and split-frozen output-sensitive subspace interventions.
entries.result: Identifies extraction-index following and output-subspace concentration under these tasks; baseline mapping competence is checked.
entries.limit: Content-versus-answer-code separation alone is already directly studied.

entries.title: How Do LLMs Perform Two-Hop Reasoning in Context?
entries.method: Three-layer synthetic model plus a reduced dynamical model and large-model distractor experiments; first-hop precedes second-hop within chains.
entries.result: Contrasts uniform guessing and sequential queries, with finetuning generalization across distractor counts.
entries.limit: Showing that distractors impair two-hop lookup is insufficient novelty. Ordered-premise causal path tests need a narrower distinction.

entries.title: LLMs Process Lists With General Filter Heads
entries.method: Uses query-state interchange and sparse head masks to test portable predicates in list filtering.
entries.result: Already describes lazy filter heads and eager item flags, including query-position dependence.
entries.limit: Generic eager/lazy strategies and predicate-versus-answer controls are already covered by actual causal interventions; order-conditioned table-join path tests still need a precise distinct claim.

entries.title: Orientation, Not Magnitude: The Causal Structure of Task-Vector Interference in Merged Language Models
entries.result: Reports BF16 rounding-dominated local generation and common-state FP32 audits in model merging.
entries.citation_correction: Claude called this Reading the Gate; the identifier resolves to the title recorded here. Do not accept that citation/title pairing without correction.

entries.title: Stochastic Rounding in Low-Precision Transformer Inference: A Variable-Precision Emulation Study of a Small GPT-2
entries.result: Site-specific rounding-rule experiments; main method body NOT_YET_READ and no fine-grained novelty ruling based on abstract.

entries.title: Float32-Induced Distortion in Activation Patching: Precision Floors and Displacement-Dependent Endpoint-Curvature Error
Hidden APIs in Language Models: Discovering Reusable Causal Interfaces from Forked Futures
entries.method: Prefix states cached before sampling future operations; shared/local/mixture/distributed codes compared under capacity and causal MDL; heldout operation/family transplants and path necessity/restoration.
entries.result: Reusable pre-future codes and selective causal transplantation are already investigated. Their ground-truth architecture audit reports a nonzero false-Shared error.
entries.limit: B cannot claim generic pre-query storage or reuse as novel. A token trajectory under a sealed modified graph differs from a learned compact interface, but exact firstness remains UNVERIFIED.

entries.title: Evaluating the Ripple Effects of Knowledge Editing in Language Models
entries.method: Six edit consequence criteria include two compositionality directions, aliasing, preservation and specificity. Also evaluates an in-context editing baseline.
entries.result: Direct edit success does not ensure derived updates. This broad question is already covered.
entries.limit: C has been narrowed to obsolete-history influence at exactly matched final tables. Hygiene controls alone do not establish novelty.

entries.title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
entries.method: Filler-content and same-composition ordering manipulations; residual patches by layer and span; probes; filler-to-prior attention knockout.
entries.result: Ordering and early-layer state affect uplift, and some filler benefits survive removing prior-context access.
entries.limit: D tests before-target ordering with opposite task selectivity and exact token multiset. This does not independently isolate abstract syntax, and generic filler gain is not novel.

entries.title: Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention in Hybrid Architectures
entries.method: Trains hybrid attention architectures under scaling budgets, separately restricts full/efficient attention receptive fields, and probes final query state on NIAH.
entries.result: Long-context performance in these trained hybrids relies mainly on full-attention access; efficient layers contribute little direct long-range retrieval gain in the tested setup.
entries.limit: Does not itself identify a natural one-token carrier in Gemma 4. B still must distinguish source refresh from stored state and modified-graph sufficiency from natural necessity.

entries.title: DERELAB: Probing Defeasible Reasoning and Confirmation Bias in LLMs with a Generative Benchmark
entries.method: Parameterized default/inheritance graphs generate multi-turn updates, source priorities, irrelevant branches, reinstatement and formal per-turn oracles. Evidence order and question order are configurable. Conversation bootstrap.
entries.result: Evaluates nine LMs including Gemma-4-12B-it; broad belief update, scope and contradiction effects are already addressed.
entries.limit: C exact final-state-matched archive manipulation is not established as new by this comparison; no abstract-only novelty clearance. Official PDF SHA b8e2d6d121507150b51f5ef55dfd4563b69046f8c36a496640f490cf9b9265d3.

novelty_rule: no firstness claims from search absence; primary method overlap determines rejection
